meta.title: Read It Out Loud
meta.skill_frame: Literary text: follow a rule one character gives another, and whether it is used.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 3.55 and 3.30 on the two parts (52 and 47 words), 3.42 together. The load is one rule and one mistake, so the reader holds the rule in memory while the second part tests it. That sits inside the grade 2-3 band and below the 4.1 floor, which measures 5.3 at its easiest.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for literary_text 3.1, band 3.1, sequence 5. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A printer and a new apprentice, built so one stated rule is broken and then used in the second part.
source.avoided: No shop name, town, or client. No claim about what the poster said.

session.difficulty_basis: One rule stated in the first part and missed in the second, with the fix left to the reader.

authoring_exceptions: Parts run 45-60 words instead of 100-200. At band 3.1 the text is short by design: two parts keep the session inside 12 minutes and the whole story stays visible on one screen. Recorded under 2.1.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The old printer sets type by hand at a small press behind the shop. He gives the new apprentice one rule on her first morning. Set the line, then read it out loud, because a line that is hard to say is hard to read. She writes the rule on the wall.
passage.part_2: The apprentice sets a poster in a hurry on Friday. She reads it in her head and tells the printer it is fine. He reads it out loud and stops at one line. She sets that line again, shorter, and the poster goes to press before six.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Set the line, then read it out loud.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The printer says: set the line, then read it out loud.
tutor_only.tell: The rule is to set the line and then read it out loud.
help: The sentence after the first morning gives the rule.
It names two things to do, one after the other.
tutor_only.core_idea: Set the line, then read it out loud.
accept_ideas: set the line and read it out loud
set the line then read it aloud
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says set the line quickly
if_they_say.ask: Speed is not in the rule. What does he say to do after the line is set?

items.prompt: What does the apprentice do instead of reading the poster out loud?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. She reads it in her head.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says she reads it in her head and tells the printer it is fine.
tutor_only.tell: She reads the poster in her head, so she never hears the line.
help: The sentence about the apprentice reading the poster says how she reads it.
It is the opposite of out loud.
tutor_only.core_idea: She reads it in her head.
accept_ideas: she reads it in her head
she does not read it out loud
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says she reads it to the printer
if_they_say.ask: The passage says she tells him it is fine. How did she read it first?

items.prompt: Why does the printer stop at one line?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. That line is hard to say out loud.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The rule says a line that is hard to say is hard to read, and he stops at one line.
tutor_only.tell: The printer stops at one line because it is hard to say out loud.
help: Look at what the rule says about a line that is hard to say.
The rule links saying and reading.
tutor_only.core_idea: That line is hard to say out loud.
accept_ideas: the line is hard to say
it is hard to read aloud
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the line is too short
if_they_say.ask: He stops before she makes it shorter. What does the rule say about a line that is hard to say?

items.prompt: She sets the line again and makes it shorter. Why does that fix it?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. A shorter line is easier to say out loud.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The rule says a hard-to-say line is hard to read, and the shorter line goes to press.
tutor_only.tell: The rule ties saying to reading. A shorter line is easier to say, so it is easier to read.
help: Connect the rule to what she changes about the line.
She makes one change, and it is about length.
tutor_only.core_idea: A shorter line is easier to say out loud.
accept_ideas: a shorter line is easier to say
short lines are easier to read aloud
it is easier to say now
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the line had a spelling mistake
if_they_say.ask: The passage mentions no spelling. What does the rule connect to reading?

items.prompt: The apprentice read the poster in her head and said it was fine. What does the story show about checking your own work?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Reading it out loud finds what reading silently misses.
tutor_only.correct_reason: She read it silently and missed the line the printer heard at once when he read it out loud.
tutor_only.tell: She read the poster in her head and heard nothing wrong. The printer read it out loud and found the line.
help: Compare how each of them read the poster.
One read it silently, and the other read it out loud.
tutor_only.core_idea: Reading it out loud finds what reading silently misses.
accept_ideas: you miss things when you read silently
the printer heard what she did not
reading it out loud is how you check your work
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the apprentice cannot read
if_they_say.ask: The passage says she read the poster. What did the printer do that she did not?
